question_text: The 35th term of an A.P. is 69. Find the sum of its first 69 terms.

mark_split.label: Write S₆₉ in terms of the 35th term

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this — say what S₆₉ turns into and why you never need a and d separately.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write S₆₉ in terms of the 35th term
steps.margin_note: First mark. 68d is exactly twice 34d, so the bracket is twice the 35th term. Do not try to solve for a and d.
steps.memory_tip: 69 terms, and the 35th is the middle one: the sum is 69 times that middle term.
lines: Sum of the first n terms:  Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d]

recall.must_convey: That S₆₉ = 69/2[2a + 68d] = 69(a + 34d), which is 69 times the 35th term.
accept: write the sum formula and take two common outside the bracket
sixty eight d is twice thirty four d
the sum of sixty nine terms is sixty nine times the thirty fifth term
sum formula rasi, bracket lo a plus thirty four d vasthundi
i do not need a and d separately
heard_as: two into a plus thirty four d

steps.why: The bracket 2a + 68d is exactly 2(a + 34d), so the whole sum collapses to 69 × a₃₅. Finding a and d is impossible here, and also unnecessary.
common_mistakes: Trying to solve a + 34d = 69 for a and d, which has no unique solution.
Writing Sₙ = n/2 [2a + nd] and losing the match with a + 34d.

steps.label: Substitute the given 35th term
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 69² = 4761. The answer coming out as a perfect square is the sign that the short route was taken.

recall.must_convey: That a + 34d = 69 is substituted to give S₆₉ = 69 × 69 = 4761.
accept: sixty nine times sixty nine is four thousand seven hundred sixty one
substitute the thirty fifth term as sixty nine
the sum is sixty nine squared
sixty nine into sixty nine, four seven six one
the answer is four thousand seven hundred and sixty one
heard_as: four thousand seven hundred sixty one

steps.why: One given number is used once, and 69 × 69 = 4761 completes the answer without ever needing a value for a or d.
common_mistakes: Halving a second time and writing 4761/2.
